missing.concept_he: יאוש / אין שום יאוש בעולם כלל
missing.concept_en: Despair (yeush) and its prohibition — 'there is no despair in the world at all'
missing.refs: LM II:78
missing.why: Zero hits for יאוש/תתיאש anywhere in 3,588 concepts. This is arguably THE flagship hitchazkut dictum of Likutey Moharan (II:78, Gevalt-ye'ush section). Both the harmful state (yeush) and the counsel against it are absent; sadness (atzvut) exists but despair does not.

missing.concept_en: Hitchazkut — spiritual self-strengthening / never giving up
missing.why: Zero hits for התחזקות. Only two narrow nodes exist (c:chizzuk-ha-lev 'strengthening the heart', c:likutey-moharan-ii 'strengthening the angel'). The general practice-concept that names an entire pillar of Breslov avodah — explicitly listed in this audit's domain scope — has no node.

missing.concept_en: Temimut u-peshitut — simplicity and wholeheartedness in serving God, without sophistication (chochmot)
missing.refs: LM II:19, II:78, II:5
missing.why: Zero hits for תמימות/פשיטות as concepts; the only hit is the Psalms epithet 'temimei darekh' (c:ps-11). LM II:19 states explicitly that the essence of serving God is temimut u-peshitut without any chochmot — a core avodah counsel with no node.

missing.concept_en: Turning Torah teachings into prayers
missing.refs: LM II:25 (end); cf. Sichot HaRan 145
missing.why: Zero hits for any form (תורות תפלות, נעשה מהתורה, etc.). This is the signature practice appended to the main hitbodedut teaching — Rebbe Nachman calls the resulting prayers 'sha'ashuim gedolim' before God. A first-order eitza missing entirely.

missing.concept_en: Spiritual descent / fall, and descent-for-the-sake-of-ascent
missing.refs: LM I:22, II:78; cf. I:6 (ratzo va-shov)
missing.why: Zero hits for ירידה; נפיל hits are epilepsy and 'their brazenness falls'. The graph has c:baki-ratzo-baki (the expertise of descent, LM I:6/II:78) but the descent-state itself — the thing every hitchazkut edge should act on — has no node, so 'fall -> hitchazkut -> return' chains cannot be expressed.

missing.concept_he: גשר צר מאד / והעיקר לא להתפחד כלל
missing.concept_en: The very narrow bridge — the counsel not to fear at all
missing.refs: LM II:48
missing.why: Zero hits for גשר צר or לא להתפחד. One of the most-cited dicta of LM II:48 (hitchazkut domain): the world as a narrow bridge and fearlessness as the essential response. Neither the image nor the counsel exists as a concept.

missing.concept_en: Hoda'ah — thanksgiving/gratitude as a devotional mode (the delight of Olam Haba)
missing.refs: LM II:2 ('ימי חנוכה הם ימי הודאה')
missing.why: Zero hits for הודאה/הודיה as a standalone concept; להודות appears only bundled inside c:ability-pray-sing. LM II:2 makes hoda'ah itself a central category (days of thanksgiving = the sha'ashua of the World to Come), distinct from prayer-of-petition.

missing.concept_en: Conducting hitbodedut in one's spoken vernacular (Yiddish)
missing.refs: LM II:25
missing.why: Zero hits for לשון אשכנז. LM II:25 makes the vernacular requirement a defining condition of hitbodedut ('because the heart is drawn after the language one is accustomed to'). Lower priority than the items above but a distinct, explicit counsel of the core hitbodedut teaching.
